description: A graduate study of how modern processors and memory systems reach high performance within power limits, from out-of-order cores and branch predictors to coherence, consistency, accelerators and hardware security. Each topic pairs derivations and simulator experiments with a critical reading of a research paper, ending in a small architecture study.
modelledOn: Hennessy and Patterson, Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach
Sorin, Hill and Wood, A Primer on Memory Consistency and Cache Coherence
Jacob, Ng and Wang, Memory Systems: Cache, DRAM, Disk
Shen and Lipasti, Modern Processor Design: Fundamentals of Superscalar Processors
outcomes: Evaluate architectural proposals quantitatively using Amdahl's law, the roofline model and sound simulation methodology.
Trace instructions through an out-of-order core with renaming, a reorder buffer and a load-store queue, and explain recovery from misspeculation.
Design and compare branch predictors, cache and prefetch policies and memory controllers using simulated workloads.
Reason about coherence protocols and memory consistency models with litmus tests and fences.
Analyse power, reliability and transient-execution security trade-offs in a processor design.
Read, critique and reproduce results from architecture research papers and present an original experiment.

units.title: Quantitative design and the research method
topics: Quantitative principles: Amdahl's law, Gustafson's law and the roofline model
Benchmarking and simulation methodology: sampling, warm-up and threats to validity
Technology trends: the end of Dennard scaling, the power wall and dark silicon
Reading architecture papers: structure, claims, evidence and a critique template
Instruction-set design choices: RISC-V base and extensions, vector instructions

units.title: Out-of-order execution and speculation
topics: Tomasulo's algorithm: reservation stations, common data bus and register renaming
Reorder buffer, precise exceptions and in-order commit
Load-store queues, memory disambiguation and store-to-load forwarding
Superscalar issue: wakeup and select, issue width and scheduling window limits
Speculation and recovery: checkpoints, flush penalties and the cost of misprediction
Paper strand: critique a classic out-of-order design paper and reproduce one table

units.title: Advanced branch prediction and the front end
topics: Two-bit counters, gshare and tournament predictors
TAGE and perceptron predictors: history lengths, tagging and training
Branch target buffers, return address stacks and indirect branch prediction
Decoupled front ends, micro-op caches and instruction prefetch
Paper strand: evaluate a predictor on traces and report mispredicts per kilo-instruction

units.title: Cache and memory system design
topics: Cache organisation, average memory access time and the three Cs of misses
Replacement and insertion policies: LRU, re-reference interval prediction and Belady's optimal policy
Hardware prefetching: stride, stream and correlation prefetchers; pollution and accuracy
Non-blocking caches, miss status holding registers and memory-level parallelism
DRAM organisation: banks, row buffers, scheduling policies and high-bandwidth memory
Virtual memory hardware: TLB design, huge pages, page walks and non-volatile memory

units.title: Multicore, coherence and on-chip networks
topics: Coherence protocols: snooping MESI and MOESI, directory-based protocols and their states
On-chip networks: mesh and torus topologies, routing, virtual channels and deadlock
Synchronisation hardware: atomics, load-linked/store-conditional, locks and transactional memory
Multithreaded and throughput cores: simultaneous multithreading and GPU warp scheduling
Paper strand: how coherence scales beyond 100 cores

units.title: Memory consistency models
topics: Sequential consistency, total store order and relaxed models (Arm and RISC-V)
Litmus tests and fences: store buffering, message passing and load buffering
Axiomatic models and the happens-before relation
Data races and language-level memory models in C++ and Java

units.title: Accelerators and domain-specific architectures
topics: SIMD and vector architectures; vectorisation limits
Systolic arrays and neural-network accelerators; data reuse and dataflow
FPGAs, coarse-grained reconfigurable arrays and high-level synthesis
Near-memory and in-memory computing
Low-cost, low-power inference hardware for edge deployments in African settings

units.title: Low-power and reliable design
topics: Dynamic and static power: voltage and frequency scaling, clock and power gating
Thermal limits, dark silicon and power-capping
Soft errors, ECC, parity and redundancy for fault tolerance
Process variation, ageing and approximate computing

units.title: Hardware security
topics: Transient execution attacks: Spectre and Meltdown mechanisms
Cache side channels: prime-and-probe and flush-and-reload
Mitigations: fences, partitioning, constant-time code and their performance cost
Rowhammer, hardware trojans and trusted execution environments

units.title: Research project and open problems
topics: Designing an architecture experiment: simulator, workload set, metrics and baselines
Reproducibility and artefact evaluation
Writing the short paper and presenting it; mock peer review
Open problems: energy-proportional computing, chiplets, memory-centric design

schedule.title: Measuring and judging architecture ideas
schedule.exercise: Apply Amdahl's law and a roofline plot to a proposed accelerator, then write a half-page critique of a short architecture paper using the claim, evidence and threats template.

tasks.title: Plot a roofline for a core with 100 GFLOP/s peak and 25 GB/s memory bandwidth and place three kernels as compute or memory bound
Run the same program on a pipeline simulator with and without warm-up and report how the cycle count and cache miss rate shift
Review a mock paper scenario with a flawed baseline and cherry-picked workloads, list its threats to validity and score your critique against a rubric

schedule.title: Register renaming and dynamic scheduling
schedule.exercise: Trace a 12-instruction sequence with RAW, WAR and WAW hazards through Tomasulo's algorithm by hand, listing the reservation stations, renamed registers and the commit order.

tasks.title: Step a ten-instruction sequence through reservation stations and the common data bus, recording each instruction's issue, execute and write-back cycle
Trigger an exception in the middle of an out-of-order window and show with the reorder buffer why the architectural state stays precise
Run a load after an earlier store with an unknown address and compare conservative, speculative and forwarding policies by cycles and replays

schedule.title: Issue width, recovery and the paper strand
schedule.exercise: Reproduce a table of IPC against window size from a classic out-of-order paper using the simulator and explain any differences from the published values.

tasks.title: Sweep the issue width from 1 to 8 and window size from 16 to 256 on one workload and identify where returns diminish
Measure the flush penalty from a mispredicted branch at pipeline depths of 8, 14 and 20 stages and fit the penalty per stage
Write a small trace-driven model of an out-of-order window in code and compare its IPC with the visualiser for three traces

schedule.title: Branch prediction from counters to TAGE
schedule.exercise: Compare gshare, tournament and a TAGE-like predictor on traces with loops, nested conditions and data-dependent branches, and report misses per thousand instructions with a short critique.

tasks.title: Run a two-bit predictor and gshare on a loop-heavy trace and report the accuracy, explaining the first mispredictions by hand
Implement a perceptron predictor with 32-bit history, train on a trace of 100000 branches, and compare accuracy with gshare at equal storage
Evaluate a return address stack of depth 4, 8 and 16 on a recursive workload and find the depth that removes all return mispredictions

schedule.title: Cache design and replacement
schedule.exercise: For a given address trace, compute hit rate for direct-mapped, 4-way and fully associative caches, classify the misses into compulsory, capacity and conflict, and compare LRU with the optimal policy.

tasks.title: Classify every miss in a 40-access trace for a 4-line cache as compulsory, capacity or conflict and compute the average access time
Implement LRU, random and Belady's optimal replacement, run a loop larger than the cache and show why LRU thrashes while others do not
Add a stride prefetcher to the cache simulator, measure accuracy and coverage on array and linked-list code, and quantify pollution

schedule.title: Memory-level parallelism, DRAM and virtual memory
schedule.exercise: Model a memory controller serving row-hit and row-miss requests, schedule a queue of 16 requests with first-come and row-hit-first policies, and compare latency and fairness.

tasks.title: Vary the number of miss status holding registers from 1 to 16 and record how execution time falls on a pointer-free array scan
Simulate a DRAM bank with open-row policy, schedule 1000 requests under two policies, and report mean latency and the worst-case wait
Compute the TLB reach for 4 KB and 2 MB pages and run a big-array scan to compare TLB miss counts and page-walk cost

schedule.title: Cache coherence
schedule.exercise: Draw state diagrams for MESI and a directory protocol and trace a sequence of reads and writes by four cores through both, counting bus messages and invalidations.

tasks.title: Trace a read-write-read sequence over three cores through MESI and record the state of each cache line and each bus transaction
Show false sharing by placing two counters in one line, count invalidations as two cores update them, and cut the traffic by padding
Model a 4x4 mesh network with dimension-order routing, inject coherence traffic, and plot latency against injection rate to find saturation

schedule.title: Synchronisation, threads and scaling
schedule.exercise: Estimate the cost of a contended lock versus lock-free update as core count grows from 2 to 64, and summarise a paper on scalable coherence in two paragraphs.

tasks.title: Implement a spinlock with test-and-set and with test-and-test-and-set, and compare bus transactions as the number of waiting cores rises
Run a memory-bound workload on a simultaneous-multithreading core with one, two and four threads and report throughput and per-thread slowdown
Critique a scalability-of-coherence paper scenario against a rubric, checking its workloads, baselines and the claim about overhead at 128 cores

schedule.title: Memory consistency
schedule.exercise: List every outcome allowed under sequential consistency and total store order for the store-buffering and message-passing litmus tests, and place the fences that forbid the odd outcomes.

tasks.title: Enumerate all interleavings of the store-buffering litmus test and list which final register values each consistency model allows
Run the message-passing litmus test 1 million times on a relaxed-order model and count the forbidden outcomes with and without a fence
Find the data race in a flag-and-data program, fix it with release-acquire atomics, and justify each memory-order choice

schedule.title: Accelerators and domain-specific design
schedule.exercise: Size a systolic array for matrix multiplication with a given on-chip memory, compute utilisation and data reuse, and decide whether a low-power edge accelerator is worth building for crop-disease detection.

tasks.title: Vectorise a loop for 4-wide SIMD, run it on the visualiser and measure speed-up, accounting for alignment and a scalar remainder loop
Simulate a 4x4 systolic array computing a matrix product cycle by cycle and report cycles, utilisation and memory reads per output
Measure inference time and energy of a small model on a Raspberry Pi and an Arduino-class board, and compare cost per inference

schedule.title: Power, thermal limits and reliability
schedule.exercise: Calculate chip power at several voltage and frequency points, decide how much DVFS saves on a bursty workload, and design an ECC scheme for a memory with a given soft error rate.

tasks.title: Compute dynamic power at three voltage and frequency pairs from the capacitance model and find the energy-optimal point for a fixed task
Encode a 4-bit word with a Hamming code, flip one bit and two bits, and show which errors are corrected or detected only
Simulate a thermal-aware throttling policy on a workload trace and measure the performance lost against a no-throttling baseline

schedule.title: Microarchitectural security
schedule.exercise: Explain step by step how a bounds-check bypass leaks a secret through a cache timing channel, and choose a mitigation by weighing its slowdown against its protection.

tasks.title: Perform a flush-and-reload on a simulated cache, time the probe accesses and recover a secret byte from the pattern of fast lines
Show with the speculation visualiser how a mispredicted branch executes a secret-dependent load and leaves a cache footprint after the squash
Apply a fence and an index-masking mitigation to a vulnerable gadget, test that the leak disappears and measure the slowdown on a benchmark

schedule.title: Architecture study, reproduction and open problems
schedule.exercise: Present a ten-minute study of one design question (predictor size, cache policy or prefetcher) with a baseline, a sweep, a reproducibility package and answers to two mock reviewer comments.

tasks.title: Choose one design parameter, sweep five values across three workloads and plot the performance and energy trade-off with a stated baseline
Package your experiment as a script with fixed seeds and a README so another student reproduces the same figure within 2 percent
Answer three reviewer comments on a mock architecture paper by running a small extra experiment and judge your response with a rubric
